clue.text: Stood up for wine

definitions.meaning: first meaning: got to one's feet, past tense of rise
second meaning: pink wine, rosé, written without its accent in the grid

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone standing up for a toast, but the two halves are separate meanings of one short word, one a verb and one a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosé is a pink wine made with brief skin contact, and the same letters form the past tense of the verb rise.

clue.text: Unhinged senatorial explanations

indicators.note: something unhinged has come off its fixings and lost its proper order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ten letters of fodder

explanation.surface: Deranged justifications offered up in a senate debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unhinged' reads as describing the explanations, but it acts on the adjective beside it; SENATORIAL rearranges into RATIONALES.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the set of reasons given for a decision or belief, so plural rationales are reasoned justifications.

clue.text: Scheming type gets artist involved

indicators.note: involved means tangled or complicated, so the letters are mixed up together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A schemer manages to draw a painter into a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets artist involved' reads as a scheme to entangle a painter; in fact GETS and ARTIST together are the ten letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategist is a person skilled at planning and plotting moves, which is exactly someone given to scheming.

clue.text: Praetorian rank to make amends

indicators.note: rank can mean foul or corrupt, so these letters are spoilt into a different order

parts.note: taken as written, ten letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A Roman guard's military rank used to atone for a wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like a noun for military grade beside Praetorian (the Praetorian Guard protected Roman emperors), but here it is the adjective meaning corrupt, signalling a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Reparation is compensation paid for a wrong or injury, the same thing as amends offered to set matters right.

clue.text: Disguises sample of flamenco Despacito

indicators.note: a sample is a small portion taken from a larger whole, so the letters come from within the words that follow

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A snippet of the Latin pop hit Despacito dressed up in flamenco style.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across the join: flam-ENCO DES-pacito. Despacito is a 2017 Spanish-language pop hit, italicised as a title.
explanation.definitionFit: To encode a message is to convert it into cipher so outsiders cannot read it, which disguises its content.

clue.text: Persistent American set on seceding in the end

parts.note: A is the standard abbreviation for American
to set, as a jelly does, is to gel
taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that last character is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A stubborn American determined to break away from the union at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set on seceding' suggests determination to leave, but set is GEL and on is simply ON; the surface echoes the US Civil War secession.
explanation.definitionFit: Something age-long lasts for a very great length of time, so it is enduring and persistent.

clue.text: Numbers present at nine balls and a cèilidh?

parts.note: taken as written
nine formal dances plus one more dance make ten of them

explanation.surface: Counting the crowd at a season of nine balls and a Scottish dance.
explanation.walkthrough: A ball is a formal dance, and a cèilidh is a Scottish or Irish social evening of folk dancing, so the clue is quietly doing arithmetic: nine of one plus one of the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Attendances are the counts of people who turn up to events, so they are the figures for those present.

clue.text: Leader of Indonesia governed country

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the word
to run a country is to govern it, past tense

explanation.surface: Indonesia's head of state ruled the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of Indonesia' sounds like a president, but it is only the first letter; the country defined is a different one.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation in western Asia, formerly known as Persia, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Require massage, you say?

indicators.note: what you say is spoken rather than written, so a word sounding the same is wanted

parts.note: to knead is to massage by working with the hands

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether they really require a massage.
explanation.walkthrough: KNEAD, with its silent K, is pronounced identically to the word meaning require.
explanation.definitionFit: To need something is to have a requirement for it; the verbs are straightforward synonyms in everyday use.

clue.text: Pungent patisserie item

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sharp or acidic in taste
second meaning: a pastry case with a filling

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like one sour cake, but the adjective and the noun phrase are separate definitions of the same four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp, acidic flavour is called tart, and a tart is also an open pastry sold in a French-style bakery.

clue.text: Account having minimal money: university worried, leading to stress

parts.note: AC is the standard abbreviation for account
a cent is the smallest unit of many currencies
U is the standard abbreviation for university
something eating at you worries you, so 'ate' means worried

explanation.surface: A student's near-empty bank account: university fees cause anxiety that brings on stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stress' looks like a noun for anxiety at the end of the story, but it is the verb meaning emphasise. 'Ate' as worried comes from 'what's eating you?'
explanation.definitionFit: To accentuate a feature is to make it more noticeable, so it is to emphasise or give stress to it.

clue.text: Starting a trip but now our Dad is lost

indicators.note: something lost has wandered astray from where it belongs, so the letters stray out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The family set off on holiday, but Dad has already got them lost.
explanation.walkthrough: The twelve letters of 'but now our Dad' rearrange into the answer; 'is lost' completes the family road-trip picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship or traveller that is outward-bound is heading away from home at the beginning of a journey.

clue.text: Campus race: I arranged for an old trophy

indicators.note: arranged means put in a particular order, so the letters are set out anew

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student organising a college race with an antique cup as the prize.
explanation.walkthrough: The America's Cup is a sailing trophy first contested in 1851, making it one of the oldest in international sport, so 'race' in the fodder is a neat touch.
explanation.definitionFit: The America's Cup is a yachting prize dating from the mid-nineteenth century, the oldest international sporting award still contested.

clue.text: Mathematician reconsidered granulation with nothing to lose

indicators.note: to reconsider is to think again and rework, so the letters are put in a new order
having something to lose means dropping it, so a letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A mathematician rethinks a grain-sized process, having nothing left to lose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with nothing to lose' sounds like a desperate gamble, but it means the O must go from GRANULATION before the remaining ten letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Turing was the British mathematician and codebreaker who founded theoretical computer science and worked at Bletchley Park.

clue.text: After hug and kiss, gaze at Tom's wife, presenting a flower

parts.note: a hug is written O, from the circle of arms
a kiss is written X at the end of a letter
to eye something is to look at it steadily
in The Great Gatsby, Tom Buchanan is married to Daisy

explanation.surface: An admirer embraces and kisses a married woman, then gazes at her while handing over a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: The hugs-and-kisses OX sign-off gives the opening letters; 'After' tells you they come first, before the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The ox-eye daisy is a tall wild plant with white petals around a yellow centre, common in meadows and verges.

clue.text: Mediterranean city is large resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, it means sort again into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A travel brochure line praising a big seaside holiday town on the Med.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' pretends to be a holiday destination, the definition's natural partner, but split as re-sort it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Algiers is the capital of Algeria, a port on the North African coast of the Mediterranean Sea.

clue.text: Not entirely dignified, sloppy serving of salmon

indicators.note: something not entirely there is incomplete, so the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: grave means solemn and dignified; its final letter is dropped
lax means careless or sloppy

explanation.surface: A waiter's slapdash plating of salmon falls short of elegance.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs 'dignified' and 'sloppy' as contrasting judgements of the serving; really they are two consecutive pieces of the dish's Scandinavian name.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravlax is a Scandinavian dish of raw salmon cured with salt, sugar and dill, served in thin slices.

clue.text: Earl against knight with legal action coming next

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for Earl
N is the chess notation for a knight
suing is taking someone to court

explanation.surface: A nobleman versus a knight, with a lawsuit on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' looks like V for versus, but here it only means next to, placing the two title letters side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensuing describes whatever follows as a result or in sequence, so it means happening afterwards or following on.

clue.text: Fancied a visitor, by the sound of it

indicators.note: judging by the sound means listening rather than reading, so the spoken form is what counts

parts.note: a guest is someone who visits

explanation.surface: Someone who seems to have taken a liking to a house guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancied' suggests attraction, but it is used in the sense of 'I fancied it might rain', meaning supposed.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something can mean to imagine or suppose it without proof, which is to make a guess.

clue.text: State of being dumb as a post?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: emptiness of mind, a blank stupidity

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'dumb as a post' fuses the halves; split it and 'a post' is a job opening, not a wooden stake.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacancy can mean vacuity or lack of intelligence, and it is also an open position waiting for someone to be hired.

clue.text: Unexciting vehicle Everyman will start to aggrandize

parts.note: a van is a road vehicle
the setter speaking of himself says I'll, I will

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: The setter promises to jazz up a dull car.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter often refers to himself by name, so 'Everyman will' is 'I will', contracted without its apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla is used figuratively for anything plain, ordinary or lacking special features, like the most basic ice-cream flavour.

clue.text: How Peter Firth may be shown to be secure, uninjured

definitions.text: How Peter Firth may be shown
definitions.meaning: first meaning, cryptic: a peter is old criminal slang for a strongbox, and a firth is a sea inlet, so each word is written as its synonym joined by 'and'
second meaning: the everyday phrase for coming through unharmed

explanation.surface: An actor's name, and how he emerged unscathed.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Firth is a real English actor, which is the disguise; splitting his name gives two words, each replaced by a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The fixed phrase describes someone who has come through danger without harm, protected and in good health.

clue.text: Addled, somewhat erratic; adrift, primarily!

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the first letter of each word is wanted

parts.note: the initial letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Someone muddled and wandering, completely at a loss.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: its first letters spell the answer, and read plainly it describes being confused and lost, which is what the answer means figuratively.
explanation.definitionFit: Asea literally means out on the ocean, and figuratively it means bewildered or confused, like a drifting boat.

clue.text: Insect's pungency brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up raises it from bottom to top, so it reads upwards

parts.note: a tang is a sharp, strong taste or smell

explanation.surface: An insect's sharp smell being mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay rather than marking possession.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a small two-winged fly, often biting, that swarms near water, so it is a kind of insect.

clue.text: Stagehands and cast learned to accommodate this ephemeral structure

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house or hold, so the words hold the answer within them

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the last of the first word to the start of the fourth

explanation.surface: The theatre crew and actors had to fit in a temporary set.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run stagehand-S AND CAST LE-arned; 'ephemeral structure' fits the stage set of the surface as neatly as the seaside answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandcastle is a model castle built on a beach that the tide soon washes away, so it is short-lived.

clue.text: Digital assistant displaying flower in retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word is read back to front

parts.note: an iris is a flowering plant

explanation.surface: A voice assistant showing a picture of a flower while withdrawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' here is a plant rather than a river, the usual crossword trick; the bloom is simply read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Siri is Apple's voice-controlled software helper on iPhones, a virtual assistant that answers spoken questions.

clue.text: Averse to humourless university official from Down Under

parts.note: anti means against or opposed to
po as in po-faced, meaning stern and humourless
a dean heads a faculty or college

explanation.surface: An Australian academic administrator who dislikes jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: PO comes from the British 'po-faced', meaning solemn and disapproving. 'Down Under' is the informal name for Australia and New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antipodes are the lands on the opposite side of the globe from Britain, chiefly Australia and New Zealand.

clue.text: Unpleasant characters regularly seen in Burghley

indicators.note: letters taken at regular intervals means every other one is picked out

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Nasty people often spotted at a grand stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: Burghley House is a large Elizabethan stately home in Lincolnshire, England, known for its horse trials; its even letters give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly can describe a situation or mood that is hostile or disagreeable, not just an unattractive appearance.
